heuristics.rule: If a 'Senior PM' offer's total comp is below the levels.fyi median for that stated level, treat it as a signal that something is misrepresented before accepting.
heuristics.condition: When evaluating an offer where the title says Senior PM but total comp is significantly below market median (e.g., $180K total vs. $350K+ median),
heuristics.action: ...verify the actual level code, not just the title, and determine whether the company has a sub-market comp culture or is back-loading equity in a way that reduces current value
heuristics.because: Title inflation is common; the level code and total comp structure reveal the true seniority and compensation band more accurately than the title alone

heuristics.rule: Use Amazon L5/L6 level codes as a translation layer when benchmarking across companies — Amazon L6 Senior PM is equivalent to Google/Meta Senior PM, not Amazon L5.
heuristics.condition: When comparing offers or leveling across Amazon and other major tech companies,
heuristics.action: ...map Amazon L6 to 'Senior PM' at Google/Meta rather than treating all 'PM' titles as equivalent
heuristics.because: Amazon's leveling nomenclature runs one step behind other companies; treating titles as equivalent without level-code mapping leads to systematic undervaluation or overestimation of seniority

heuristics.rule: Treat signing bonus size ($50K–$150K at FAANG) as a proxy for how much unvested equity you are leaving behind at your current company.
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether a signing bonus in a new offer is generous or merely standard,
heuristics.action: ...calculate your unvested equity cliff at current employer and compare it against the signing bonus being offered to determine if the switch is financially net-positive in year one
heuristics.because: Signing bonuses are structurally designed to cover unvested equity left behind; a mismatch means you are absorbing real financial loss that compounds over the vest schedule

heuristics.rule: At FAANG, negotiate equity and signing bonus first — these are the most negotiable components and where the largest dollar variance occurs.
heuristics.condition: When entering compensation negotiation at a major tech company for a Senior PM role,
heuristics.action: ...anchor negotiation on RSU grant size and signing bonus rather than base salary, since base has a narrower band and equity/signing are where companies have more flexibility
heuristics.because: Base salary ranges are rigid and constrained by band; RSU grants and signing bonuses are deal-closing tools companies use with more discretion

heuristics.rule: Non-FAANG Principal PM comp can match FAANG Senior PM comp — do not automatically assume FAANG is the only path to top-quartile compensation.
heuristics.condition: When a Senior PM is evaluating whether to join or stay at a non-FAANG company like Intuit versus pursuing a FAANG role,
heuristics.action: ...compare total comp at the target level (e.g., Principal PM at Intuit ~$482K) directly against FAANG Senior PM benchmarks (~$528K at Google L5) before assuming FAANG is materially better
heuristics.because: At senior individual contributor levels, well-compensated non-FAANG companies are competitive with FAANG; the prestige premium does not always translate to a compensation premium

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The same dollar value of equity has different real-world value depending on vesting cadence, cliff length, and refresh schedule — quarterly vesting (Meta) provides far higher liquidity than annual cliff structures
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask for the full vesting schedule, whether there are annual refresh grants, and whether the company vests monthly, quarterly, or annually after the cliff; calculate what you would actually receive in years 1 and 2

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Title inflation means a 'Senior PM' offer at one company may correspond to a lower level band than the same title at another; the level code determines the compensation band and career progression track
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request the internal level code explicitly (e.g., L5 at Google, L6 at Amazon, IC5 at Meta) and cross-reference against levels.fyi median for that specific level code

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Equivalent roles pay materially more in NY/SF than Seattle or Austin; a role that appears below market may simply reflect a location adjustment, or a role that appears competitive may be inflated by location
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Filter levels.fyi data by the specific metro area of the role; compare NY/SF comp to Seattle or Austin benchmarks for the same level to isolate the location effect

decision_factors.factor: Stock price trajectory of the offering company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RSU grants are quoted at current stock price but vest over 4 years; a company whose stock declines 40% over the vest period delivers far less than the stated total comp
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate the company's stock performance trajectory, refresh grant policies, and whether the company reprices or issues additional grants during downturns

decision_factors.factor: Market timing — entry-level vs. senior-level demand
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The current market (2024–2025) is strong for Staff/Principal PM roles but compressed for entry and mid-level; this asymmetry changes negotiation leverage and job availability depending on where you are in your career
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess your current level against where hiring demand is concentrated; if you are at Senior+ with 7–10 years at quality companies, leverage is high; if you are APM or early PM, supply exceeds demand

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Amazon's historically cash-heavy structure at L5/L6 provides more predictable income but lower upside compared to Google or Meta's equity-heavy structures; personal financial situation affects which mix is preferable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate your personal financial need for liquid cash income versus tolerance for equity risk; compare the base + bonus cash component across offers before factoring in equity

decision_factors.factor: Refresh grant timing and performance rating cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Total comp at a company like Meta or Google compounds significantly if you receive strong performance ratings that trigger above-band refresh grants; a flat performer at the same level receives materially less over time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask about the refresh grant process, how performance ratings translate to equity refresh, and what the typical range of refresh grants looks like at the target level

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a high-total-comp offer at a company with equity-heavy, back-loaded vesting
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Year 1 and Year 2 actual cash-in-hand is significantly lower than the stated total comp figure; the headline number is only realized if you stay through the full vest and the stock price holds
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs who have financial obligations in the near term or who overweight the headline total comp number without modeling year-by-year cash flow

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Choosing Amazon L6 for its cash-heavy compensation structure
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Lower equity upside means you miss disproportionate gains if the company's stock appreciates significantly; the stability premium costs you asymmetric upside that equity-heavy companies provide
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs who are financially stable and could tolerate equity risk but defaulted to cash certainty without fully pricing the opportunity cost

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a non-FAANG 'Senior PM' title without verifying compensation against FAANG benchmarks
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You may be accepting a title that sounds equivalent but carries a compensation band 30–50% below what the same title commands at a major tech company, with no clear path to close that gap internally
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs who optimize for title over compensation band, particularly those early in their Senior PM tenure who anchor on the prestige of the title

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Joining a FAANG as an entry-level or early PM in the 2024–2025 market
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: APM and early PM hiring has compressed significantly; the pathway that was viable in 2021 is now far narrower, meaning candidates are competing for fewer spots while senior roles remain open — the market is bifurcated, not uniformly strong
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: New graduates and early-career PMs who assume the FAANG PM market is as accessible as it was during the 2021 hiring peak

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Prioritizing base salary negotiation over equity negotiation at FAANG
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You leave the largest dollar variance on the table because base salary bands are rigid and the incremental gain from base negotiation is a fraction of what a better RSU grant or signing bonus would yield
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs who are less experienced with equity negotiation or who are uncomfortable with variable income and therefore anchor on the most tangible, predictable number

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting an offer based on title without verifying the level code and corresponding compensation band
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Title inflation is pervasive and companies exploit the ambiguity; candidates anchor on titles they recognize ('Senior PM') without probing the internal level taxonomy that determines actual comp and career trajectory
failure_patterns.consequence: PM accepts a role underpaid relative to their actual market value and seniority, with limited internal recourse to correct the band mismatch without leaving
warning_signs: Offer total comp is materially below levels.fyi median for the stated title
The hiring manager or recruiter is vague or evasive when asked for the internal level code

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating the stated total comp figure as equivalent to annual take-home pay
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Total comp figures combine cash, equity, and bonuses in a way that flatters the annual number; candidates unfamiliar with RSU vesting mechanics conflate the grant value with realized income
failure_patterns.consequence: PM is financially surprised in year 1 and year 2 when actual cash received is significantly below expectations, sometimes creating real financial strain if they made decisions (e.g., housing) based on the headline figure
warning_signs: PM cannot articulate how much of their total comp vests in year 1 vs. year 4
PM has not modeled a scenario where the stock price drops 30% over the vest period

failure_patterns.pattern: Benchmarking compensation against the overall median ($229K) rather than the relevant level and company tier
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The overall market median includes mid-market, startup, and FAANG roles across all levels; using it as a reference point systematically underestimates what senior PMs at major tech companies should expect
failure_patterns.consequence: PM undervalues their offer or fails to negotiate aggressively because they believe market median is $229K when their actual relevant benchmark is $400–600K
warning_signs: PM cites overall market median as their compensation anchor during negotiation
PM has not filtered levels.fyi data by company, level code, and location before forming an opinion on what is fair

failure_patterns.pattern: Conflating Amazon's level nomenclature with other companies' and accepting an L5 role when targeting Senior PM equivalency
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Amazon's PM titles do not map cleanly to the rest of the industry; L5 at Amazon is 'PM' while L6 is 'Senior PM' at Google/Meta equivalency — candidates who don't know this accept a lower level than intended
failure_patterns.consequence: PM joins Amazon at a level below their actual seniority, accepts a lower compensation band, and must spend additional years re-earning a promotion to achieve the level they already held at their prior company
warning_signs: PM is targeting a Senior PM role and receives an Amazon offer without independently verifying whether it is L5 or L6
Recruiter uses title 'Product Manager' without specifying the level code during initial discussions

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the internal level code for this offer, not just the title?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the title reflects the actual seniority band the company uses internally for compensation and promotion purposes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Cross-reference the level code against levels.fyi median total comp for that specific code at that company — does the offer match?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Treat the lack of a clear level code as a red flag and push the recruiter to specify it before proceeding with compensation discussion

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the year-by-year vesting schedule, and are there annual refresh grants?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Your actual realized income in years 1 through 4, which may be dramatically different from the headline total comp figure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Model the cash flow scenario with and without stock price appreciation to understand the range of outcomes you are actually accepting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If there are no refresh grants, the total comp degrades significantly in years 3 and 4 after the initial grant vests — this changes the long-term value of the offer substantially

diagnostic_questions.question: How does this offer compare to the levels.fyi median filtered by company, level code, AND metro area?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the offer is below-band, at-band, or above-band for your specific situation — the unfiltered median is not a useful benchmark
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the offer is at or above median, determine whether there is still room to negotiate equity and signing bonus upward before accepting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the offer is below median after filtering, determine whether this reflects a negotiation gap (addressable) or a structural comp culture issue at the company (less addressable)

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the signing bonus, and does it cover your unvested equity at your current company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the financial switch is net positive or net negative in year one after accounting for equity you are leaving on the table
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If signing bonus exceeds unvested equity, the switch is financially safe in year one — evaluate the multi-year comp trajectory next
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If signing bonus does not cover unvested equity, calculate the break-even point and determine whether the long-term comp upside justifies the short-term loss

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the role at a FAANG or equivalent major tech company, or a non-FAANG large tech company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you should benchmark against FAANG comp tables or non-FAANG benchmarks, since conflating them leads to systematic misvaluation in either direction
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Use company-specific levels.fyi data for Google, Meta, Amazon, or LinkedIn rather than aggregate PM salary data
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Compare against Intuit-equivalent benchmarks; note that Principal PM at strong non-FAANG can match FAANG Senior PM total comp, so do not automatically assume FAANG is superior

industry_realities.common_belief: The PM job market is strong right now, so entry-level and senior PMs are both in high demand.
industry_realities.actual_reality: The market is bifurcated: Staff and Principal level PMs with 7–10 years at quality companies are in high demand, but APM and entry-level PM hiring has compressed significantly since the 2021 peak and remains tight in 2024–2025.
industry_realities.implication: Early-career PMs should not assume the same market conditions that made APM programs accessible in 2021 still apply; they are competing for fewer spots while senior PMs have leverage they may not be fully using

industry_realities.common_belief: FAANG always pays more than non-FAANG, so joining a major tech company is the only path to top-quartile PM compensation.
industry_realities.actual_reality: At senior individual contributor levels (Principal PM and above), well-compensated non-FAANG companies like Intuit pay in the same range as FAANG Senior PM — Intuit Principal PM median is ~$482K versus Google Senior PM median of ~$528K.
industry_realities.implication: PMs should evaluate non-FAANG Principal PM roles on total comp merit rather than dismissing them as inferior; the FAANG prestige premium does not always translate to a meaningful compensation premium at senior levels

industry_realities.common_belief: A higher total comp number means you will take home more money annually.
industry_realities.actual_reality: Total comp is a blended figure that includes equity that vests over 4 years, signing bonuses that are one-time, and bonuses that are performance-contingent; actual year-1 take-home is often materially lower than the headline total comp figure.
industry_realities.implication: PMs must model year-by-year realized income rather than dividing total comp by four; the structure of when equity vests and whether refresh grants exist changes the actual financial trajectory significantly

industry_realities.common_belief: Negotiating base salary is the most impactful lever in a compensation negotiation.
industry_realities.actual_reality: At FAANG, base salary bands are rigid and have a narrow range; equity (RSU grant size) and signing bonus are where companies have the most flexibility and where the largest dollar variance occurs.
industry_realities.implication: PMs should anchor their negotiation energy on RSU grant size and signing bonus, treating base salary as a secondary lever; focusing primarily on base salary leaves the most money on the table

industry_realities.common_belief: Amazon 'Senior PM' and Google 'Senior PM' are equivalent roles at equivalent levels.
industry_realities.actual_reality: Amazon's leveling runs one step behind: Amazon L5 is equivalent to 'PM' at Google/Meta, and Amazon L6 is equivalent to 'Senior PM' at Google/Meta. A candidate who accepts an Amazon PM offer (L5) when they held a Senior PM title elsewhere has effectively accepted a demotion in level band.
industry_realities.implication: Always verify the Amazon level code before comparing offers or accepting; do not treat 'Senior PM' title equivalency across companies without checking the internal level code

industry_realities.common_belief: The overall PM market median salary ($229K) is a reliable benchmark for evaluating whether an offer is fair.
industry_realities.actual_reality: The $229K median includes all levels, all company types, and all geographies blended together; Senior PM at FAANG in a major metro has a relevant benchmark of $400–600K+ in total comp, making the overall median useless as a negotiation anchor.
industry_realities.implication: Always filter compensation benchmarks by company, level code, and metro area before forming a view on whether an offer is fair; using the overall median systematically undervalues Senior PM offers at major tech companies

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Uses overall PM market median ($229K) or generic salary ranges from broad job sites as their reference point; does not filter by company, level code, or location
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Filters levels.fyi data by the specific company, internal level code, and metro area before forming any view on whether an offer is fair or what to negotiate toward
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Using the wrong benchmark causes PMs to under-negotiate or accept below-market offers; the overall median can be 50–70% below the actual relevant benchmark for a Senior PM at FAANG

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Evaluates an offer by looking at the headline total comp number and dividing by four to estimate annual income
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Models year-by-year realized income accounting for vesting schedule, cliff structure, refresh grant eligibility, signing bonus one-time nature, and stock price sensitivity
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Headline total comp can be misleading by 30–50% in early vest years; a PM who doesn't model year-by-year cash flow makes decisions based on income they may not actually receive

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Anchors negotiation on base salary because it is the most tangible and predictable component; views equity negotiation as secondary or uncomfortable
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats base salary as the least flexible lever and directs negotiation energy toward RSU grant size and signing bonus, which have the highest dollar variance and most company flexibility
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A PM who focuses on base salary negotiation at FAANG might gain $10–20K; the same energy directed at equity and signing bonus can yield $50–150K+ in incremental value

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Takes job titles at face value and assumes 'Senior PM' means the same level and band at every company
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Immediately asks for the internal level code and translates it against known benchmarks (e.g., knows Amazon L6 = Google L5 = Meta IC5 for Senior PM equivalency)
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Accepting a title without verifying the level code can result in joining a company at a lower level than your prior role, with a lower comp band and longer time to the next promotion

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Assumes the PM job market is uniformly strong or uniformly weak based on headline narratives about tech layoffs or hiring booms
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Recognizes the market is bifurcated: senior-level PM roles (Staff/Principal) are in demand with strong leverage, while entry and mid-level PM hiring is compressed — and calibrates job search strategy and negotiation posture accordingly
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A senior PM who doesn't recognize their leverage in the current market will under-negotiate; an early PM who assumes the 2021 market still exists will be surprised by how competitive and limited APM pathways have become
